chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Look at the children who are with you, and send them to Al-Juhfa or to Batin Marra, and do with them what is done with the Muhrim (one in Ihram), circumambulate with them, and throw stones on their behalf. And whoever among them cannot find a sacrifice, let his guardian fast on his behalf. And Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) would place the knife in the hand of the child, then a man would hold his hands, so he would slaughter.

key_terms.بَطْنِ مَرٍّ: Batin Marra (a Miqat station for Hajj)
key_terms.بِالْمُحْرِمِ: with the Muhrim (one in the state of Ihram)

ai.seo_question: How is Hajj performed for young children who have not reached religious maturity?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the juristic principle that young children are exempt from the personal obligation of Hajj but participate in its rituals through representation, mirroring the status of those in Ihram. It highlights the practical application of the guardian's role, specifically detailing the physical guidance of the child's hand during the slaughter of the sacrificial animal (Hady). The ruling provides a fallback mechanism where the guardian fasts if a sacrificial animal is unavailable, reflecting the flexibility in Shia fiqh for minors' religious duties.
